text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident opened: GPU prefill OOM spike affecting model-serving-prod-us-east-1. Severity: pager.

Priya S (oncall-sre): getting pages, seeing rapid container restarts on pool-gpu-4. Pods entering CrashLoopBackOff after prefill on long context requests.

Marta L (eng-runtime): logs show repeated OOM during prefill stage, kernel message: "[E] GPU OOM while allocating 7.2GB for KV cache prefill". Stack looks like runtime/prefill.cpp:prefill_tokens().

James K (eng-sre): node flapping on 10.4.2.12 — kubelet reporting containerd OOM kill then node NotReady briefly. Could be memory pressure cascading.

Priya S (oncall-sre): PagerDuty acknowledged by Priya. Triage: Are these requests unusually large? Any customer escalations? @Aisha R please check active customers hitting this cluster.

Aisha R (cs): Seeing an enterprise customer spike with very long system prompts + 150k-token user traces via streaming prefill. Customer reported degraded latency and multiple failed responses. They confirm heavy batch of historical context ingestion.

Liu W (eng-ml): This workload will blow past usual KV cache assumptions. Prefill currently doesn't trim or guard on total prefill tokens for some back-compat routes.

Marta L (eng-runtime): Quick mitigation options: 1) enable prefill_token_cap per-route (hotpatch), 2) route heavy requests to CPU-fallback queue, 3) deploy model-variant with aggressive quantization and lower KV usage. Which is fastest?

Priya S (oncall-sre): Hotpatch 1 looks fastest. Can we flip a config flag without full restart?

Marta L (eng-runtime): Yes — config flag prefills.max_tokens_per_request exists and can be toggled via configmap; runtime reads it on SIGHUP. I'll prepare a hotpatch.

James K (eng-sre): While Marta prepares, I'll cordon node 10.4.2.12 and drain pods to stop flapping spread. Command I'll run: `kubectl cordon node/10.4.2.12 && kubectl drain node/10.4.2.12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`

Cameron P (support): Noted. Customer-facing update queued: "We're throttling oversized prefill requests to protect service stability; we'll follow up with root cause and timeline." Do we have ETA?

Marta L (eng-runtime): Preparing configmap patch now. Patch will set `prefills.max_tokens_per_request: "40000"` and `prefill.trim_strategy: "stream_trim_enabled"` for prod cluster. Applying to namespace model-serving-prod.

incident-bot: Deploy started: configmap patch prefills-hotpatch by Marta L.

Marta L (eng-runtime): Pushed patch, issuing SIGHUP to runtime pods via `kubectl rollout restart daemonset/runtime-gpu` one node at a time to avoid mass restarts.

Priya S (oncall-sre): Observability: enabling token-level sampling and prefill metrics dashboard now, turning on debug logs for prefill module for 30m.

James K (eng-sre): Node cordon+drain completed for 10.4.2.12. Re-scheduled pods on healthy nodes with capacity. Monitoring OOM count.

Liu W (eng-ml): Also enabling soft-kludge: route requests with estimated prefill > 45k tokens to fallback-model-vsmall which uses lower KV and batch footprint. I pushed routing rule via feature flag.

Priya S (oncall-sre): After hotpatch, we're seeing a drop in OOMs. Container restarts per minute fell from ~18 to 2 over the last 6 minutes.

Marta L (eng-runtime): Logs excerpt from a failing pod before patch:
```
I0312 09:12:15.123 runtime: prefill start id=abcd1234 user=acct-6789 tokens=152345
E0312 09:12:15.456 cuda: cudaErrorLaunchOutOfResources in conv_kernels.cu: kernel launch failed
E0312 09:12:15.457 runtime: failed to allocate 7458765312 bytes for kv_cache prefill: out of memory
W0312 09:12:15.458 containerd: oom event, process pid=4521 killed
```

Priya S (oncall-sre): Thanks. Post-patch logs show similar requests being rejected with 413 Payload Too Large or gracefully routed to fallback: `prefill_rejected: token_count_exceeds_route_cap`.

Aisha R (cs): Customer notified: initial message sent with apology and mitigation steps. Customer asked for timeline on durable fix and whether historical ingestion can be throttled client-side.

Marta L (eng-runtime): Next steps for durable fix: 1) server-side prefill token estimator at edge to prevent oversized prefill from reaching GPU runtime; 2) persistent route-level caps and backpressure; 3) better streaming-trim heuristics to reduce front-loaded KV pressure.

James K (eng-sre): I'll keep nodes cordoned until we confirm no regression. Autoscaler alerting to be adjusted to avoid scaling into unhealthy nodes.

Priya S (oncall-sre): Handoff plan: I'll remain on the thread for 30m while we stabilize then hand to second oncall (James) for monitoring. Please add short postmortem once RCA is clear.

incident-bot: Pager update: assigned to Priya S, severity lowered to degraded after hotpatch.

Cameron P (support): Noted — customer update posted to their ticket. Will follow up with recommended client-side throttling patterns and suggested prefill limits.

Liu W (eng-ml): I'll open a PR for estimator and a unit test suite simulating 100k-token prefill to validate rejection behavior.

Priya S (oncall-sre): Current status: Service stable, OOMs near zero. Keeping debug logs for 20 more minutes. If no new OOMs, we'll demobilize.

Aisha R (cs): Customer acknowledged and appreciates quick mitigation. Asking for a timeline for the permanent fix; I'll share roadmap notes from Liu/Marta when available.

Marta L (eng-runtime): Will draft RFC for permanent fixes (edge estimator + trim heuristics) and link here.

Priya S (oncall-sre): Handoff to James in 22 minutes for monitoring. Thank you all. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident closed for paging, monitoring-only. Final note: cause flagged as unbounded prefill token bursts causing KV cache over-allocation; mitigated by route caps and fallback routing.
